reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) only shows that CALPHAD can model phase equilibria in CrCoFeMnNi and that protective oxides like Al2O3 and SiO2 are desirable, but it provides no specific prior data on segregation, diffusion limitation, or coherent scale formation in CrFeCoNiAl/Si. The key mechanistic premises are unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Selective segregation of Al or Si to the metal/oxide interface occurs in CrFeCoNiX alloys at high temperature
This segregation limits interdiffusion of oxygen and metal ions at the interface
Limited interdiffusion enables nucleation and parabolic growth of a coherent, protective alumina or silica scale
The coherent scale blocks further transport, preventing stress accumulation and spallation
CALPHAD and DFT can predict the relevant diffusion coefficients and interface energies
